title: Burst latency pocket table — Meera
content:
Purpose: super-small personal tracker to capture short burst runs (10–200 requests) focusing on prefix/KV cache hit behavior, batching tradeoffs, and quick cost estimates. Use this to decide whether to enable prefix caching + small batch pooling for user-facing low-QPS endpoints.

Columns:
Run ID | Date | Model | Quant | Batch | Prefix Cache Hit % | Avg token latency (ms) | 95th token latency (ms) | Throughput (tok/s) | Cost per 1k tokens (est) | Prompt len | Notes / anomalies | Next action

R-2026-001 | 2026-01-14 | redwood/gpt-small-v2 | int8 | 1 | 0% | 9.2 | 28.5 | 110 | $0.35 | 32 | cold-starts, no cache; single-request perf baseline | try micro-batching 2
R-2026-002 | 2026-01-14 | redwood/gpt-small-v2 | int8 | 4 | 0% | 10.8 | 36.1 | 320 | $0.18 | 32 | batching adds queue/multiplex overhead but increases throughput | test async prefetch
R-2026-003 | 2026-01-15 | redwood/gpt-small-v2 | int8 | 4 | 65% | 6.1 | 18.3 | 480 | $0.12 | 30 | prefix cache warmed for 65% of tokens; big latency wins | measure cold-to-warm transition time
R-2026-004 | 2026-01-16 | redwood/gpt-medium-v1 | q4_0 | 2 | 40% | 8.7 | 30.2 | 260 | $0.22 | 48 | q4 quant reduces cost; tail latency still noisy | profile GPU kernel occupancy
R-2026-005 | 2026-01-16 | redwood/gpt-medium-v1 | q4_0 | 8 | 80% | 5.4 | 14.9 | 1100 | $0.09 | 46 | high cache hit + big batch -> best token/unit cost but higher p95 for first token | try dynamic batching policy
R-2026-006 | 2026-01-20 | redwood/gpt-large-v1 | fp16 | 1 | 0% | 25.9 | 120.3 | 40 | $1.10 | 64 | large model single-request expensive; cold KV miss | consider capping large-model on host tier
R-2026-007 | 2026-01-21 | redwood/gpt-large-v1 | fp16 | 2 | 55% | 14.2 | 46.7 | 160 | $0.62 | 60 | decent improvement with partial KV reuse | run 10-run sweep with randomized prefixes

Quick observations (notes-to-self):
- Prefix cache hit drives most of the avg-token latency improvements for medium/large models (duh) but warm-up behavior is critical for UX.
- Micro-batching (2–4) sometimes raises avg latency when cache cold; but once warmed, it gives huge throughput gains and lowers cost/unit.
- For low-QPS interactive endpoints, invest in a small LRU prefix cache with short TTL (30s) + opportunistic prefetch for flagged users.
- Quantization (q4_0) reduces cost but kernel scheduling can increase p95; need kernel-level profiling on p95 cases (GH#827).

Hypotheses to test next (short checklist):
[ ] Measure time-to-80%-cache-hit after first request for typical user session (3 prompts, 20–60 tokens each).
[ ] Sweep batch sizes {1,2,4,8} with simulated arrival patterns: burst (20 reqs/sec for 5s), steady low (0.5 reqs/sec), and poisson.
[ ] Try TTLs {15s,30s,60s} and track memory + hit% tradeoff.
[ ] Compare prefetch: none vs prefetch next token (cheap heuristic) vs prefetch next prompt (risky).

Lightweight formulas I use here:
- throughput (tok/s) ~ (avg tokens per request * requests per sec) measured by collector (not derived)
- cost per 1k tokens = (cost_per_gpu_sec / gpu_tokens_per_sec) * 1000 approximated from observed throughput + billing estimator

Quick calc examples (for notes):
- R-2026-003: avg tok latency 6.1ms -> ~164 tok/s per request stream; observed parallel throughput 480 tok/s across batch.
- R-2026-005: cost per 1k tokens ~$0.09 (quant + high prefix reuse) -> target to keep below $0.12 for mid-tail deployments.

Links / refs:
- personal trace dashboards: /dashboards/meera/kv-cache-bursts (internal)
- GH PR for kernel profiling: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/827
- ticket: JIRA-INF-4123 (batching policy edgecases)

Next immediate steps (today):
- run 20-run sweep for R-2026-005 conditions (q4_0, batch 8) with randomized prompt lengths (10–80 tokens) and attach traces. Owner: Meera.
- summarize p95 behavior in 1-pager and share with Arjun + Ivy.

Notes-to-self meta: keep this compact — move stable runs to the team sheet if cleaned. This file intentionally noisy (timestamps, TODOs, half calculations).
